note: Regions claim a known, accepted difference between ps-flow and upstream, and
carry the written reason for it plus a ticket when it is a known bug. This
file is where the boundary module's own regions are recorded as they are
created; the gate that consumes them — with the rule that an empty region
fails as stale, so a region outlives its cause by exactly one run — lands with
the net's comparison core (issue #40) and its self-consistency and driving-log
checks (issue #43). Recording them at the moment the divergence is introduced
rather than when the reader exists is the point: a region is someone's stated
decision, and the person who can state it is the one making the change.
`fields` is a list of paths into an observed value. It is deliberately not a
trace-section pattern yet — the trace's seven-section shape is issue #40's to
define, and inventing half of it here would give that ticket a schema to work
around rather than one to fill in.

reason: ps-flow's internal Node and Edge records make these seven Booleans
required where upstream leaves them optional, so the boundary emits them
on every node and edge it hands back. Upstream passes the consumer's own
object through and simply has no such key. The values are never wrong —
an unset Boolean crosses as `false`, which is what upstream's own readers
default it to — so this is a shape difference, not a behaviour one.
The ordering was settled deliberately: `Maybe`-ifying the seven is an
internals refactor, and doing it before the boundary lands puts churn
ahead of the first green signal on the JS surface. It happens once the
net's `props` and `dom` sections are green, and the stale-region rule is
what forces it — this entry fails the run after the fix lands.
regions.retires_when: System.Types.Node.NodeBaseRow and System.Types.Edge.EdgeBase make these seven fields Maybe

reason: The same shape as the seven Booleans, one field along: `NodeBaseRow`'s
`measured` is a required record, so a node crossing outbound always
carries `measured: { width, height }` with both members possibly
`undefined`, where upstream's node has no `measured` key until the node
has actually been measured.
Recorded separately from the Booleans because it retires separately: the
fix is `Maybe` on the record rather than on its members, and a reader who
sees one region fail should not have to work out which half of it moved.
An optional field the consumer did not set crosses outbound as the key
present with the value `undefined`, not as an absent key. Upstream's node
and edge objects are the consumer's own, passed through untouched, so an
unset field is genuinely not there.
Deleting the undefined keys in the converter was rejected: it is a
content-aware filter, and the spec keeps those out of capture and in
normalization where they are visible. Normalization may delete by name,
which is exactly the right instrument if the maintainer decides these are
noise; until then they are a claimed difference rather than a hidden one.
`undefined` and not `null` is deliberate and is the closer of the two:
the prop objects upstream builds itself — `NodeProps` above all — do have
every key present with `undefined` for the unset ones.
regions.retires_when: normalization deletes undefined-valued keys by name, or the records become Maybe-free
